To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of the pyronin Y stain in conjunction with the Hoechst 33342 and rhodamine 123 stains provides a method for the isolation and characterization of the functional subpopulations of stem cells within the Hoechst3334lo/rhodamine123lo (H33342lo/R123lo) population of primitive hemopoietics stem cells.

the pyronin Y staining of the Hoechst333342(lo) rhodamine123(low) primitive hemopoetic stem cells (HSC) can be used as a marker of the proliferative activity of the stem cells, and that the pyronine Y staining of the HSCs is heterogeneous, indicating that the stem cells have different proliferative activity.

pyronin Y staining is a simple and rapid method of detecting the presence of functional primitive hemopoietically stem cells in the marrow of normal and leukemic patients, and that this method can be used to identify the presence of functional hemopoietically primitive cells in the marrow in patients with myelodysplasia and myelofibrosis.
